steps.hook: POV: you're in a group chat IRL and your throat locks shut.

steps.alt_text: Man standing apart from a group of people dark cinematic. Overlay text...

steps.caption:
Going mute in a group doesn't mean you have nothing to say. It means your body decided it was safer to say nothing at all.
One-on-one your nervous system only has to track one person. In a group it counts every pair of eyes at once and treats it like a trial. So your throat tightens, your chest locks, and you sit there watching the conversation move without you again.
If you rehearse a line, miss the window, and spend the night replaying how you sat there silent while everyone else looked effortless, you're not alone. Comment SEEN and I'll send you the full breakdown.

steps.hook: POV: you cancel plans and your chest finally stops racing.

steps.alt_text: Man alone on couch at night dark room cinematic. Overlay text reads: P...

steps.caption:
That relief you feel right after canceling doesn't make you a bad friend. It makes you someone whose body was bracing all day for a test.
Social anxiety doesn't fear the plan, it fears being exposed during it. So your system begs you to escape, you get relief, then shame rushes in to punish the relief. It's a loop, not a character flaw.
If you make plans you want to want, cancel them, feel calm for an hour, then feel guilty about the calm, you're not alone. Comment FREE and I'll send you the full breakdown.
